title: Alleppey Travel Guide  - Best Places to Visit in Kerala’s Venice of the East
content:
Alleppey - The Venice of the East

Alleppey, also known as Alappuzha, is one of the most beautiful tourist destinations in Kerala. Popularly called the “Venice of the East”, Alleppey is famous for its backwaters, houseboats, beaches, temples, and lush green landscapes. It is a dream destination for travelers who want to experience peace, natural beauty, and authentic Kerala culture.
Alleppey (Alappuzha) is more than just a backwater destination -  it is the soul of Kerala tourism.  Click here for Alleppey Package

Here’s why Alleppey should be on your travel list:

  • The Backwater Capital of India - Alleppey is world-renowned for its scenic backwaters, offering travelers a peaceful and unforgettable houseboat cruise experience.
  • Stay in Traditional Houseboats - Spending a night on a Kerala houseboat in Alleppey is a bucket-list activity, complete with traditional food, calm waters, and starry skies.
  • Beaches & Lagoons - Apart from backwaters, Alleppey also offers serene beaches like Alleppey Beach and Marari Beach, perfect for relaxation and sunsets.
  • Rich Culture & Festivals - Witness the Nehru Trophy Snake Boat Race, Onam celebrations, and local temple festivals that showcase the cultural vibrancy of Kerala.
  • Ayurveda & Wellness Tourism - Alleppey is home to some of the best Ayurveda spas and wellness retreats, making it ideal for healing and rejuvenation.
  • Bird Watching & Nature Trails - Vembanad Lake and Pathiramanal Island attract migratory birds, making Alleppey a paradise for bird lovers and nature photographers.
  • Authentic Kerala Cuisine - Alleppey is known for its delicious seafood, especially Karimeen Pollichathu (Pearl Spot Fish), prawns, and Kerala-style curries served on banana leaves.
  • Village Life & Heritage - From coir-making units to paddy fields, Alleppey gives travelers a taste of Kerala’s authentic rural lifestyle.
  • Perfect for All Travelers - Whether you are on a honeymoon, family trip, or solo journey, Alleppey offers something for everyone.
  • Gateway to Kerala Backwater Tourism - Alleppey is the starting point for many backwater cruises, connecting travelers to Kumarakom and Kuttanad – the “Rice Bowl of Kerala.”

Best Places to Visit in Alleppey

Alleppey Backwaters - For boating and houseboat cruises.
Alleppey Beach - Calm and scenic beach with a historic pier.
Vembanad Lake - The largest lake in Kerala, perfect for bird watching and boat rides.
Krishnapuram Palace - A historic palace with Kerala-style architecture and murals.
Marari Beach - A serene and less crowded beach near Alleppey.
Pathiramanal Island - A paradise for bird lovers.

Best Time to Visit Alleppey

November to February: Pleasant weather, perfect for sightseeing and houseboat stays.
June to September (Monsoon): Great for lush greenery and Ayurveda treatments.
March to May: Hot but good for budget travelers.

Things to Do in Alleppey

Stay in a houseboat for a unique overnight experience.
Enjoy an Ayurvedic massage.
Watch the snake boat race if you visit in August.
Try delicious Kerala seafood.
Explore villages, paddy fields, and coir-making units.
excerpt: Alleppey is truly the heart of Kerala’s backwaters and a must-visit destination. Whether it’s a romantic houseboat stay, a relaxing Ayurvedic therapy, or a walk along the golden beaches, Alleppey offers an unforgettable experience for every traveler.

faqs.question: Which is better - Alleppey or Kumarakom?
faqs.answer: Both are beautiful, but Alleppey is better for houseboat stays and backwater cruises, while Kumarakom is more peaceful and popular for luxury resorts and bird watching.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Alleppey?
faqs.answer: The best time to visit Alleppey is from November to February, when the weather is pleasant for sightseeing, houseboat stays, and beach visits. Monsoon (June–September) is perfect for Ayurveda treatments.

faqs.question: How many days are enough for Alleppey?
faqs.answer: A trip of 2 to 3 days is enough to enjoy houseboat stays, Alleppey Beach, Vembanad Lake, Marari Beach, and local village experiences.

faqs.question: How do I reach Alleppey?
faqs.answer:
By Air: The nearest airport is Cochin International Airport (75 km).
By Train: Alleppey has its own railway station well-connected to major cities.
By Road: Good bus and taxi connectivity from Kochi, Trivandrum, and other parts of Kerala.

faqs.question: What is Alleppey famous food?
faqs.answer: Alleppey is known for its Kerala-style seafood, especially Karimeen Pollichathu, Alleppey Fish Curry, prawns, and traditional Kerala Sadhya.
